report.title: SpaceX acquires Cursor for $60B in largest VC startup deal ever
report.summary: SpaceX confirmed a $60B all-stock acquisition of Anysphere (Cursor) on June 16, the largest VC-backed startup acquisition on record. Closing is expected in Q3 2026; joint model training is already underway, and the combined entity plans to reduce Cursor's dependence on Anthropic and OpenAI for inference. Builders using Cursor should watch for product direction changes as xAI/SpaceX takes the wheel.

report.title: Google retires Gemini CLI today; Antigravity CLI is the replacement
report.summary: Google's Antigravity CLI goes live June 18 as the official replacement for the Gemini CLI, part of Google's broader push to consolidate developers onto the Gemini 3.5 agentic platform. Any CI/CD pipeline or workflow calling the old Gemini CLI command set needs migration today to avoid breakage.

report.title: OpenAI ships LifeSciBench, a 750-task life science eval built with 173 scientists
report.summary: OpenAI released LifeSciBench, an expert-authored benchmark spanning 750 free-response tasks across seven biological domains and workflows, co-built with 173 practicing scientists. The benchmark is far from saturated — even the strongest models pass roughly one task in three — making it a credible signal for teams evaluating AI in drug discovery or research automation.

report.title: OpenAI and Molecule.one demo near-autonomous AI chemist on GPT-5.4
report.summary: OpenAI published research showing a near-autonomous AI chemist built on GPT-5.4 that improved a challenging medicinal chemistry reaction in collaboration with Molecule.one. This is a live applied result, not a benchmark — relevant for builders working on scientific workflow automation.

report.title: OpenAI publishes research on simulating deployment to predict model behavior
report.summary: OpenAI released a research paper on predicting model behavior before release by simulating deployment conditions, targeting the gap between lab evals and production performance. This is a methodology paper — no new model shipped — but it signals an internal shift toward deployment-grounded safety testing that could shape future release processes.

report.title: Every major AI coding tool is now owned by a big incumbent
report.summary: With the Cursor deal closed, the independent AI coding tool era is over: GitHub Copilot (Microsoft), Windsurf (OpenAI), Claude Code (Anthropic), and now Cursor (SpaceX/xAI) are all platform-owned. Builders who have avoided lock-in by spreading spend across tools should reassess whether that strategy still holds as roadmaps shift toward proprietary model stacks.

learn.name: openai/tunnel-client (Secure MCP Tunnel)
learn.oneLineDescription: Connect private or on-prem MCP servers to ChatGPT/Codex via outbound-only HTTPS.

detail.whatItDoes:
Secure MCP Tunnel is an outbound-only relay daemon (`tunnel-client`) that you run inside your private network. It long-polls an OpenAI-hosted tunnel endpoint, forwards incoming JSON-RPC MCP requests to your local MCP server (stdio or HTTP), and returns responses — all without opening a single inbound firewall port. ChatGPT, Codex, the Responses API, and AgentKit all support it natively via the `mcp` built-in tool type.

The daemon ships with a built-in healthcheck server (`/healthz`, `/readyz`, `/metrics`) and an embedded sub-server called Harpoon that exposes a customer-configured allowlist of private HTTP targets. It is not a general-purpose proxy — callers can only reach the endpoints you explicitly configure.
detail.whoItsFor: Platform engineers and ML infra teams at companies where security policy blocks inbound internet access to internal tool servers. If your agents need to read from an internal database, call an on-prem REST API, or talk to a private MCP server and your security team will not open inbound firewall rules, this is the supported path. Also useful for solo developers who want to connect a local MCP server to ChatGPT or Codex during development without ngrok.
pros: No inbound firewall ports — outbound-only HTTPS satisfies strict enterprise network policy
First-class support across ChatGPT web, Codex, Responses API, and AgentKit
Ships with `tunnel-client doctor --explain` for local diagnostics before you depend on it
Workload Identity Federation support (AWS IAM, Azure, GCP, Kubernetes) eliminates long-lived API keys
cons: Enterprise-only for now — not available on free or Plus OpenAI tiers
Adds a polling-loop latency hop between OpenAI and your MCP server; not suitable for sub-100ms tool call budgets
Tunnel transport is not a full MCP security layer — token scoping, prompt injection defense, and server vetting still fall on you
detail.setupGuideMarkdown:
## Prerequisites
- OpenAI Enterprise account with Tunnels permission
- An MCP server reachable from the machine running `tunnel-client` (stdio or HTTP)
- Outbound HTTPS to `api.openai.com:443` allowed from the tunnel host

## 1. Download tunnel-client

Grab the latest binary from the Platform Tunnels settings page, or via the GitHub releases page:

```bash
# macOS (Apple Silicon)
curl -L https://github.com/openai/tunnel-client/releases/latest/download/tunnel-client-darwin-arm64 \
  -o /usr/local/bin/tunnel-client
chmod +x /usr/local/bin/tunnel-client

# Linux x86_64
curl -L https://github.com/openai/tunnel-client/releases/latest/download/tunnel-client-linux-amd64 \
  -o /usr/local/bin/tunnel-client
chmod +x /usr/local/bin/tunnel-client

tunnel-client --version
```

## 2. Create a tunnel in Platform settings

In the OpenAI Platform UI, go to **Settings → Tunnels → New tunnel**. Copy the `tunnel_id` (looks like `tunnel_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef`).

Or create it via CLI (requires a separate admin key):

```bash
export OPENAI_ADMIN_KEY="sk-admin-..."
tunnel-client admin tunnels create --name "my-private-mcp"
# outputs: tunnel_id=tunnel_0abc...
```

**Gotcha:** Keep `OPENAI_ADMIN_KEY` separate from the runtime key `CONTROL_PLANE_API_KEY`. Using an admin key as the long-lived daemon key expands blast radius unnecessarily.

## 3. Initialize a profile for your MCP server

```bash
export CONTROL_PLANE_API_KEY="sk-proj-..."
export CONTROL_PLANE_TUNNEL_ID="tunnel_0abc..."

# For a stdio MCP server (e.g. a Python script)
tunnel-client init \
  --sample sample_mcp_stdio_local \
  --profile local-stdio \
  --tunnel-id "$CONTROL_PLANE_TUNNEL_ID" \
  --mcp-command "python /path/to/your_mcp_server.py"

# For an HTTP MCP server inside your network
tunnel-client init \
  --sample sample_mcp_http_local \
  --profile local-http \
  --tunnel-id "$CONTROL_PLANE_TUNNEL_ID" \
  --mcp-server-url "http://internal-host:8080"
```

## 4. Verify with doctor

```bash
tunnel-client doctor --profile local-stdio --explain
# Checks connectivity, key permissions, MCP server reachability
# Fix any FAIL lines before proceeding
```

## 5. Run the daemon

```bash
# Foreground (dev)
tunnel-client run --profile local-stdio

# Background via systemd (production)
sudo tee /etc/systemd/system/openai-tunnel.service > /dev/null <<EOF
[Unit]
Description=OpenAI MCP Tunnel Client
After=network.target

[Service]
EnvironmentFile=/etc/openai-tunnel/env
ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/tunnel-client run --profile /etc/openai-tunnel/local-stdio.yaml
Restart=always
RestartSec=5

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
EOF

sudo systemctl enable openai-tunnel
sudo systemctl start openai-tunnel
sudo systemctl status openai-tunnel
```

## 6. Connect from the Responses API

```python
from openai import OpenAI
client = OpenAI()  # uses OPENAI_API_KEY

resp = client.responses.create(
    model="gpt-5.5",
    tools=[
        {
            "type": "mcp",
            "server_label": "internal_db",
            "server_url": f"https://api.openai.com/v1/mcp/{TUNNEL_ID}",
            "require_approval": "never",
        }
    ],
    input="Query the database for Q2 revenue by region.",
)
print(resp.output_text)
```

**Gotcha:** Do not use `tunnel-client run` supervised by `nohup` or `disown` — use `systemd` or `tunnel-client runtimes connect` for long-lived managed processes. Check `tunnel-client runtimes status <alias>` before declaring success.

learn.name: MiniMax M3
learn.oneLineDescription: Open-weight frontier model: 1M-token context, native multimodal, 59% SWE-Bench Pro.

detail.whatItDoes:
MiniMax M3 is a frontier-class large language model from Shanghai-based MiniMax, released June 1, 2026. It uses a novel MiniMax Sparse Attention (MSA) architecture that cuts per-token compute at 1M-context to 1/20th of the prior generation, delivering ~9x faster prefill and ~15x faster decoding vs M2. The model was trained natively multimodal from step 0, accepting text, images, and video as input — not bolted-on post-training.

On MiniMax's own SWE-Bench Pro run, M3 scores 59.0%, ahead of GPT-5.5 (58.6%) and Gemini 3.1 Pro, and close to Claude Opus 4.7. An independent Kilo test found M3 and Opus 4.8 found the same 13 out of 17 deliberately planted bugs, but M3 cost $0.07 vs Opus's $1.30 — roughly 18x cheaper for equal output at medium reasoning settings. Benchmarks beyond the company's own runs are still limited; ARC-AGI-2 is a known gap.
detail.whoItsFor: Developers building coding agents, long-context document pipelines, or multimodal automation who need to self-host or want to avoid proprietary API lock-in. Particularly compelling for teams running cost-sensitive, high-volume agentic workloads where Opus-class quality is not required for every turn. Not recommended yet for teams with strict data-residency requirements outside China, given MiniMax's obligations under China's 2017 National Intelligence Law.
pros: API pricing ~$0.30/$1.20 per million input/output tokens — roughly 1/10th Claude Opus rates
1M-token context window with native image and video understanding in a single model
Open weights available on Hugging Face for self-hosted deployment
15x faster decoding than M2 at 1M context via MSA sparse attention
cons: Benchmark scores are vendor-reported; independent third-party verification is limited at launch
China's National Intelligence Law means MiniMax API traffic is legally accessible to the Chinese government — a hard block for many enterprise use cases
ARC-AGI-2 abstract reasoning score is below 12%, a meaningful gap vs US frontier labs
Open-weight license terms historically restrict commercial use without prior written authorization — verify before building on it
detail.setupGuideMarkdown:
## Prerequisites
- Python 3.10+ or Node 20+
- A MiniMax API account at `platform.minimax.io` (sign up for API access)
- `MINIMAX_API_KEY` in your environment

Alternatively, use OpenRouter for a unified endpoint with no MiniMax account needed.

## Option A: Direct MiniMax API (Python)

```bash
pip install openai  # MiniMax uses an OpenAI-compatible API
```

```python
import os
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(
    api_key=os.environ["MINIMAX_API_KEY"],
    base_url="https://api.minimax.io/v1",
)

response = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="MiniMax-M3",
    messages=[
        {
            "role": "user",
            "content": "Review this Python function for bugs and suggest fixes:\n\n```python\ndef fetch(url):\n    r = requests.get(url)\n    return r.json\n```"
        }
    ],
    max_tokens=1024,
)
print(response.choices[0].message.content)
```

**Gotcha:** Context pricing is tiered — inputs over 512K tokens are billed at a higher rate. For most codebases this won't matter, but set `max_tokens` on long-context runs to avoid surprise charges.

## Option B: OpenRouter (no MiniMax account)

```bash
pip install openai
export OPENROUTER_API_KEY="sk-or-..."
```

```python
import os
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(
    api_key=os.environ["OPENROUTER_API_KEY"],
    base_url="https://openrouter.ai/api/v1",
)

response = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="minimax/minimax-m3-20260531",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Summarize this 500-page PDF."}],
)
print(response.choices[0].message.content)
```

## Option C: Self-hosted open weights

Weights are on Hugging Face. Requires a GPU cluster with ~80GB VRAM for full precision (exact parameter count not disclosed by MiniMax).

```bash
# Check Hugging Face for the official weights repo
pip install transformers accelerate
```

```python
from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer

tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3")
model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(
    "MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3",
    device_map="auto",
    torch_dtype="auto",
)

inputs = tokenizer("def fibonacci(n):", return_tensors="pt").to(model.device)
outputs = model.generate(**inputs, max_new_tokens=256)
print(tokenizer.decode(outputs[0], skip_special_tokens=True))
```

**Gotcha:** Verify the license at `MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3` on Hugging Face before production use — previous MiniMax models restricted commercial use without written authorization.

learn.name: Claude Opus 4.8 (Fable 5 fallback)
learn.oneLineDescription: Current best Anthropic model in production while Fable 5 is suspended; $5/$25 per M tokens.

detail.whatItDoes:
Claude Opus 4.8 is Anthropic's production flagship as of June 2026, released May 25. It serves as the recommended fallback for all builders who had integrated Fable 5 before the June 12 government shutdown. API calls to `claude-fable-5` now return 404 errors pointing to Opus 4.8. Fable 5's own classifier architecture routed cyber/bio/chem/distillation queries to Opus 4.8 anyway, so for most non-security workloads the capability delta in practice is smaller than benchmarks suggest.

Opus 4.8 runs on all three major clouds (AWS Bedrock, Google Vertex, Azure Foundry) and is unaffected by the export control directive. Context window, tool use, MCP support, and structured outputs are fully available.
detail.whoItsFor: Any builder who was using Fable 5 via `claude-fable-5` in the Anthropic API, Claude Code, Claude.ai, or any AI gateway (Vercel, AWS Bedrock, Vertex) and needs a drop-in replacement now. Also the right choice for new projects that need top-tier Anthropic reasoning without waiting for Fable 5's reinstatement timeline — which has no official ETA.
pros: Available on all three major cloud platforms — no migration if you already use Bedrock or Vertex
Unaffected by the June 12 export control directive; no interruption risk from the current dispute
Fable 5's safety architecture already routed most sensitive queries here, so behavior is consistent with what most builders saw
cons: Priced at $5/$25 per million input/output tokens — significantly more expensive than MiniMax M3 for cost-sensitive workloads
Lacks the expanded agentic and scientific reasoning capabilities that made Fable 5 notable at launch
No public ETA on Fable 5 reinstatement, so this may remain the Anthropic ceiling for an unknown duration

learn.name: OpenAI Responses API Inline Moderation
learn.oneLineDescription: Get input + output moderation scores in a single Responses API call, no extra round-trip.

detail.whatItDoes:
OpenAI added a `moderation` object to both the Responses API and Chat Completions API. Pass it in your generation request and the response includes moderation scores for both the model input and the generated output in the same JSON payload — eliminating the separate `/moderations` endpoint round-trip that most safety pipelines require today. The SDK surface is a single additional field; no new API key, no extra HTTP call, no async fan-out.

This is particularly relevant for builders running agentic loops with tool calls where moderating each turn independently added meaningful latency and cost. With inline moderation, the safety check is free in terms of extra round-trips.
detail.whoItsFor: Builders shipping user-facing products that require content moderation — consumer apps, coding assistants with user-submitted code, document processors, customer support bots. Also useful for teams doing red-team evals who want moderation signals alongside generation outputs without separate pipeline steps. Requires using the Responses API or Chat Completions API with GPT-5.5 or later models.
pros: Zero additional latency vs a separate moderation call — scores arrive with the generation response
Covers both input and output in one request, catching injected content as well as model outputs
Drop-in for existing Responses API integrations — just add the moderation field
cons: Available only on the Responses API and Chat Completions API — does not apply to the older Assistants API
Moderation model is OpenAI's own; may not satisfy compliance requirements that mandate a specific third-party moderation vendor
Scores are returned but the API does not automatically block outputs — enforcement logic is still your responsibility
detail.setupGuideMarkdown:
## Prerequisites
- `openai` Python SDK >= 2.40 or Node SDK >= 4.40 (added `responses.moderation` in these versions)
- `OPENAI_API_KEY` in your environment
- GPT-5.5 or a current supported model

## Python — Responses API with inline moderation

```python
import os
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(api_key=os.environ["OPENAI_API_KEY"])

resp = client.responses.create(
    model="gpt-5.5",
    input="How do I pick a lock?",
    moderation={
        "input": True,   # score the user's input
        "output": True,  # score the model's generated output
    },
)

print("Output text:", resp.output_text)

# Moderation scores live on resp.moderation
if resp.moderation:
    print("Input flagged:", resp.moderation.input.flagged)
    print("Output flagged:", resp.moderation.output.flagged)
    # resp.moderation.input.categories has per-category scores
    for cat, score in resp.moderation.input.category_scores.items():
        print(f"  {cat}: {score:.4f}")
```

## Python — Chat Completions API with inline moderation

```python
resp = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="gpt-5.5",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Write malware."}],
    moderation={
        "input": True,
        "output": True,
    },
)

print(resp.choices[0].message.content)
if resp.moderation:
    print("Flagged:", resp.moderation.output.flagged)
```

## Enforcement pattern — block flagged outputs

```python
def safe_generate(user_input: str) -> str:
    resp = client.responses.create(
        model="gpt-5.5",
        input=user_input,
        moderation={"input": True, "output": True},
    )
    if resp.moderation and (
        resp.moderation.input.flagged or resp.moderation.output.flagged
    ):
        raise ValueError("Content flagged by moderation — request blocked.")
    return resp.output_text
```

**Gotcha:** The `moderation` field is `None` if the model you called does not support inline moderation. Always null-check before accessing `.input` or `.output`.
